title: They attended Trump's controversial meme coin dinner. It didn't go well
description:
Trump held another meme coin dinner for top holders of his cryptocurrency — an event that has raised intense controversy. Here's an inside account from two guests who attended.

JUANA SUMMERS, HOST: With Democrats winning majorities in Congress, President Trump will likely face investigations into the billions of dollars he and his family have made in crypto. Despite that, the president held another dinner last night to reward the top holders of his meme coin, a cryptocurrency he launched right before his inauguration. NPR's Rafael Nam talked with two people who were there.RAFAEL NAM, BYLINE: Crypto investor Morten Christensen was among the over a hundred guests who gathered at Trump's golf club on a damp evening in Northern Virginia. He was there to attend what was promoted as the most exclusive dinner in the world. He brought along his little sister. They rode together in an Uber.MORTEN CHRISTENSEN: Yeah. I'm excited. It's always nice to dress up for an event. My sister looks amazing.NAM: Christensen has attended these events before. This time, it was a lot less expensive. The coin has cratered in price. By using a sophisticated trading strategy, he says they were basically going for free. His sister, Gabrielle Felen, was decked out in a nice black dress.GABRIELLE FELEN: Yeah. I'm also excited, a little bit nervous, but excited about how it's going to be.NAM: Christensen and Felen have agreed to share voice memos through the night, and the three of us buckled in for the event. Trump's crypto events are controversial. The top holders of the coin get to spend time with the president. The more you buy, the closer the access. In the past, many of the attendees have not been from the U.S., raising concerns that Trump could be influenced, which the White House denies. Inside the swanky gala room, Christensen rattles off the people he's met.CHRISTENSEN: One was from Saudi. One was from London. Met a couple of people from Ukraine, two people from India, four from China. I think one was from South Korea.NAM: Christensen and Felen are also from abroad, from the Netherlands. They say it's not Trump's politics that drew them to the event. Christensen even believes meme coins are stupid, but it was a chance to see the leader of the free world up close and mingle with guests like Kevin O'Leary from "Shark Tank." But just as they got there, things started taking a turn. He thought he was on the VIP list.CHRISTENSEN: I got into the entrance, and they said, I'm not on the VIP list, even though I have the email of VIP and everything, and they just said, I'm not on the list, so...NAM: And just as they started getting ready for the president to walk in, a couple of people approached Christensen. He was getting kicked out for posting pictures online and talking to people in the media, like me. He ended up all the way outside the golf club in the middle of soaking rain.CHRISTENSEN: So I got removed from the event, from the Trump gala. I'm not sure why.NAM: NPR did not get a response from organizers as to why. At the golf course, they both decided Felen would stay. She had come all this way to see the president, and she finally got the moment she was waiting for.UNIDENTIFIED MUSICAL ARTIST: (Singing) God bless the USA.(CHEERING)UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: Long live Donald Trump.PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: Do you want to hear another one (ph)? Should we keep the song going?UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: Yeah.NAM: Trump went on to deliver a speech that veered everywhere, from crypto to digs on Biden - a speech that Christensen never got to hear.CHRISTENSEN: It happens, you know. It's a different kind of experience this time around - could have been better for me. But I will just laugh about it.NAM: Felen enjoyed hearing Trump, but she also felt for her brother.FELEN: I was definitely disappointed for him, especially when, later, I saw that some people who were in VIP actually got, like, a one-on-one selfie with Trump, so probably also got to shake his hand, say some words. So that would have been a great opportunity.NAM: As they departed the U.S., Christensen and Felen weren't as excited anymore. Like many who have purchased the Trump meme coin, they had a different feeling - disappointment.Rafael Nam, NPR News.(SOUNDBITE OF MUSIC) Copyright © 2026 NPR. All rights reserved.
